display_name: Macrina, sister of Basil the Great

names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 19 iulie, «Sfânta Cuvioasă Macrina, sora Sfântului Vasile cel Mare», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Ιουλίου, «Οσία Μακρίνα αδελφή του Μεγάλου Βασιλείου», with the rank word and the kinship clause left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 19. јул ст. ст., „Преп. Макрина.“ — «Преп.» is the rank word and is left off by §6, and the heading gives no epithet and no by-name at all, so the bare forename is the whole of the form. **The heading offers nothing to tell her from her grandmother**, which is why `foldchk.py` returns `[(’macrina-the-elder’, ’sr’)]` for this string and why the fold is read in this batch’s commit message rather than avoided: there is no fuller Serbian form on the page to reach for.

Name page 2580 of days.pravoslavie.ru is «Макрина Каппадокийская, Новая, Младшая, прп.»; the rank is stripped and the three epithets kept in the page's order. The day line declines her as «Макрины , сестры свт. Василия Великого» and gives no epithet at all.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 июля ст. ст. — «Прп. Макрины , сестры свт. Василия Великого (380).»

attestations.note: The day's first entry and the same menologion day as the folder's Romanian, Greek and Serbian rows. Name page 2580 is «Макрина Каппадокийская, Новая, Младшая, прп.» — Cappadocia, and «Новая» and «Младшая», the New and the Younger, which tell her from her grandmother of the same name; the display name tells her by her brother instead and was NOT changed. `dates` UNCHANGED, AND THE YEARS DISAGREE BY ONE: the line closes «(380)» where the folder holds 379 off saint.gr's heading «(324 - 379)». The reading life4264 was NOT opened, nor id373, which is Basil's own page and is linked here only because the line names him as her brother; NO ROW WAS WRITTEN FOR BASIL, the entry being hers. THREE HYMNS TAKEN and the second of them is THE VENERABLE WOMAN'S COMMON, «В тебе, мати, известно спасеся», printed with her name set into it, which BRIEF.md §4 says is her service and is copied whole.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 19 iulie — «Sfânta Cuvioasă Macrina, sora Sfântului Vasile cel Mare»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Ιουλίου — «Οσία Μακρίνα αδελφή του Μεγάλου Βασιλείου»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and «Οσια Μακρινα Αδελφη Του Μεγαλου Βασιλειου (324 - 379)» is the folder's own woman: the elder sister of Basil the Great and Gregory of Nyssa, raised by her mother Emmelia, betrothed to a man who died, withdrawn with her mother to a women's monastery in Pontus by the river Iris. She is not `macrina-the-elder`, her grandmother, whom the corpus keeps on 30 May. The page's heading gives the years the Romanian source did not and they are taken into `dates`. It also lists her relics: part of the right foot at the Monastery of Iviron on Athos, part of the left hand at the Monastery of Panachrantou on Andros, a part at Stavronikita on Athos, and a portion at Kykkos in Cyprus. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints two apolytikia and both are taken: the first names her, and the second is the common of a venerable woman, «Ἐν σοὶ Μῆτερ ἀκριβῶς διεσώθη τὸ κατ᾽ εἰκόνα», printed under her name with her name in its closing line, so it is her service and not a mis-hang.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.08.2026 (19. јул ст. ст.) — „Преп. Макрина.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop (§4). «Преп.» is the `venerable` this folder already carries, so nothing is read off the heading into `types`, and «Св.» does not appear in it at all. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND FOR ONCE BECAUSE TWO BOOKS AGREE TO THE YEAR.** The folder holds `birth` 324 and `death` 379 off saint.gr, and this entry ends „Упокоји се у Господу 379. год.“ — she reposed in the Lord in the year 379, the same number. Nothing is widened and nothing is narrowed; this is the first row of this day whose silence on `dates` is agreement rather than refusal. **THE FOLD THIS FORM MAKES, AND IT IS TWO WOMEN OF ONE HOUSE.** `foldchk.py` measured «Макрина» as already held in sr by `macrina-the-elder`, and `sr-foldpred.mjs` answered `new key, other holders: 1 macrina-the-elder`, so the fold is two wide and is read in this batch’s commit message. **The two are grandmother and granddaughter**: `macrina-the-elder` is kept on the 30 May by the Romanian and Serbian calendars, is `righteous`, is dated to the 4th century, and relates `basil-the-elder` and `gregory-the-wonderworker-of-neocaesarea`; this woman is the eldest sister of Basil the Great, daughter of Emilia, dated 324 to 379. **Both owe their Serbian form to this same book**, which prints the one name for both of them and nothing beside it, and that is the whole of why the fold exists. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND IT IS HER OWN VOICE TWICE OVER. The two other books in this folder tell her life through Gregory’s letter and through saint.gr’s summary of it; THIS ONE IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE THREE THAT QUOTES HER. As a virgin she was betrothed early to a young man of good birth, and when her betrothed died she vowed never to marry: „Но када њен обручник умре, Макрина се заветова никада не ступати у брак говорећи: „није право да девојка, обручена једном веренику, иде за другога; по закону природном треба да буде једно супруженство као што је једно рођење и једна смрт“.“ — it is not right that a girl betrothed to one bridegroom should go after another; by the law of nature there should be one marriage as there is one birth and one death. SHE JUSTIFIED IT BY FAITH IN THE RESURRECTION, reckoning her betrothed not dead but alive in God, and said „„Грех је и срамота, вели, да супруга не сачува верности, када јој супруг оде у неку далеку страну.““ — it is a sin and a shame for a wife not to keep faith when her husband has gone away into some far country. THEN SHE AND HER MOTHER TOOK THE HABIT TOGETHER, „По том заједно са својом мајком Емилијом прими монаштво у неком девичком манастиру, где се подвизаваху са другим инокињама.“, in a convent of virgins where they struggled with the other nuns, LIVING BY THE LABOUR OF THEIR OWN HANDS and giving the greater part of their time to the thought of God. HER MOTHER DIED, AND THEN HER BROTHER BASIL; AND IN THE NINTH MONTH AFTER BASIL’S DEATH GREGORY CAME TO VISIT HER AND FOUND HER ON HER DEATHBED. Her dying prayer is given whole: „„Ти Господе упокојаваш телеса наша сном смрти на неко време, па ћеш их опет пробудити последњом трубом. Прости мене и дај ми да кад се душа свуче од телесне одеће, предстане Теби непорочна и без греха и да буде као тамјан пред Тобом“.“ — thou, Lord, layest our bodies to rest in the sleep of death for a time and wilt wake them with the last trumpet; forgive me, and grant that when the soul is stripped of the body’s clothing it may stand before thee undefiled and without sin, and be as incense before thee. AND SHE SIGNED HERSELF ON BROW, EYES, FACE AND HEART AND BREATHED OUT: „По том направи руком крсни знак на челу, на очима, на лицу, на срцу и – издахну.“. NO NEW `related`, AND ONE RECIPROCAL SUPPLIED. The entry names Basil the Great, Gregory of Nyssa and the mother Emilia, and all three are already `related` on this folder; `proseprobe.mjs` reported `gregory-of-nyssa` as **OWES back**, so the reverse row goes in with this batch and nothing else in that folder is touched. The betrothed who died is nobody’s folder. No `office`. No `locations`: the convent is „неком девичком манастиру“, some convent of virgins, and the book names no place at all on this day. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Întru tine, maică, cu osârdie s-a mântuit cel după chip; că, luând crucea, ai urmat lui Hristos; şi lucrând, ai învăţat să nu se uite la trup, căci este trecător; ci să poarte grijă de suflet, de lucrul cel nemuritor. Pentru aceasta şi cu îngerii împreună se bucură, Cuvioasă Maică Macrina, duhul tău.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfintei Cuvioase Macrina, sora Sfântului Vasile cel Mare», Glasul 8 — the common of a woman ascetic.

english.text: In you, mother, what was made in God's image was saved with diligence; for taking up the cross you followed Christ, and by your works you taught us to overlook the body, since it passes away, and to care for the soul, a thing immortal. Therefore your spirit rejoices together with the angels, venerable mother Macrina.

hymns.text: Σοφίας ἔρωτι, τὸν νοῦν πτερώσασα, κόσμου εὐπάθειαν, ἔμφρονως ἔλιπες, καὶ ἐνδιαίτημα τερπνὸν ἔγενου θείας ἀγάπης· σὺ γὰρ δι' ἀσκήσεως, καὶ ἠθῶν τελειότητας, νύμφη ἔχρηματισας, τοῦ Σωτῆρος περίδοξος· ὦ πρέσβευε ὑπὲρ τῶν βοώντων χαίροις Μακρίνα θεοφόρε.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος γ’, Τὴν ὡραιότητα — the first of the two hymns on the page of «Οσία Μακρίνα αδελφή του Μεγάλου Βασιλείου», and it names her

english.text: Having given your mind wings by the love of wisdom, you wisely left the comfort of the world and became a delightful dwelling of divine love; for by ascetic labour and by perfection of manners you were made the Saviour's bride and were greatly glorified. Intercede, then, for those who cry: rejoice, God-bearing Macrina.

hymns.text: Ἐν σοὶ Μῆτερ ἀκριβῶς διεσώθη τὸ κατ᾽ εἰκόνα· λαβοῦσα γὰρ τὸν σταυρόν, ἠκολούθησας τῷ Χριστῷ, καὶ πράττουσα ἐδίδασκες, ὑπερορᾷν μὲν σαρκός, παρέρχεται γάρ· ἐπιμελεῖσθαι δὲ ψυχῆς, πράγματος ἀθανάτoυ· διὸ καὶ μετὰ Ἀγγέλων συναγάλλεται, Ὁσία Μακρίνα τὸ πνεῦμά σου.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’ — the second of the two hymns on the page of «Οσία Μακρίνα αδελφή του Μεγάλου Βασιλείου». It is the common of a venerable woman, printed under her name and naming her in its closing line

english.text: In you, mother, the image of God was kept exactly; for you took up the cross and followed Christ, and by your deeds you taught that the flesh is to be overlooked, since it passes away, and that the soul is to be cared for, being a thing immortal. Therefore your spirit rejoices with the angels, venerable Macrina.

hymns.text: Жениха твоего смерть видевши,/ разсмотрела еси тленную жизнь и суетие мира,/ отвсюду вину приимши,/ Нетленному Обручнику уневестилася еси,/ постом и смирением любовь Того постигающи./ Тем ныне радуется со Ангелы, преподобная Макрино, дух твой.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 июля ст. ст. — «Тропарь преподобной Макрины, сестры святителя Василия Великого», глас 2

english.text: Seeing the death of thy bridegroom, thou didst look upon the corruptible life and the vanity of the world, and taking occasion from every side thou wast betrothed to the incorruptible Bridegroom, attaining His love by fasting and humility. Therefore thy spirit now rejoices with the angels, O venerable Macrina.

hymns.text: В тебе, мати, известно спасеся, еже по образу:/ приимши бо Крест, последовала еси Христу/ и, деющи, учила еси презирати убо плоть, преходит бо,/ прилежати же о души, вещи безсмертней./ Темже и со Ангелы срадуется, преподобная Макрино, дух твой.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 июля ст. ст. — «Ин тропарь преподобной Макрины, сестры святителя Василия Великого», глас 8 — the venerable woman’s common, printed whole under her name with her name set into it

english.text: In thee, O mother, that which is according to the image was surely saved: for taking up the cross thou didst follow Christ, and by thy deeds thou didst teach us to despise the flesh, for it passes away, but to care for the soul, a thing immortal. Therefore thy spirit rejoices with the angels, O venerable Macrina.

hymns.text: Бога Благаго всем сердцем возлюбила еси,/ Макрино преподобная,/ и, Сего Крест Честный на рамо приемыш,/ усердно последовала еси Ему,/ отонудуже согрешений обрела еси прощение.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 июля ст. ст. — «Кондак преподобной Макрины, сестры святителя Василия Великого», глас 4

english.text: Thou didst love the good God with all thy heart, O venerable Macrina, and taking His honourable cross upon thy shoulder thou didst follow Him eagerly; whence thou didst find forgiveness of sins.

birth.note: saint.gr prints the years in its heading for her, «Οσια Μακρινα Αδελφη Του Μεγαλου Βασιλειου (324 - 379)». The Romanian source the folder was built from, Gregory of Nyssa's letter to Olympius as doxologia.ro prints it, gave no year of birth or death.
